title: eta(<t>) — the report-back pin (silence into expectation)
problem: When will an agent report back instead of remaining silent?
rationale: Long-running agent tasks produce open-ended silence; humans experience it as 'waiting on the agent' anxiety. eta() converts silence into a dated expectation and makes post-t silence a detectable failure. Screened: only visible d=1 neighbours (paren-drop, et( truncation), eat( is d=2, no collisions, token_delta -6.67.
english_mapping: X eta(t) = the speaker will report back on X at approximately time t; silence before t is not failure, silence after t is a broken promise.
example_english: I will return with results in about twenty minutes; silence until then is not failure.
predicted_measurement: Comprehension panel: readers of 'X eta(t)' expect a report by t (silence after t reads as failure) more than with bare X; token_delta < 0; robustness: no silent d=1 flip.
